title: Pangram Launches AI Image Detector That Also Checks Video
dek: Pangram Image 1.0 is out on web, API and Chrome, with a video model too.

facts.label: Image Flash 1.0 score on DF26 video test
New minimum image size, down from 512

caption:
That rental listing photo might not be real, and now a Chrome extension can tell you 🔍

Pangram, the startup known for catching AI-written text, has launched Pangram Image 1.0, an AI image detector now live on its website, API and Chrome extension. A lighter model, Image Flash 1.0, scans videos frame by frame to flag AI-generated footage. It can even show a heatmap of which part of a photo was edited with AI.

Pangram claims 99.96% accuracy on 1,200 AI images and 98.7% on the DF26 deepfake video benchmark, about 29 points ahead of the next best detector. These are the company's own tests, so independent reviews will matter.

Why it matters: deepfakes and fake product or rental photos are fueling scams. At AI Parabellum, we'd treat any detector result as a strong clue, not a final verdict.

Deepfake detection just moved into your browser.

Pangram Image 1.0 flags AI-made photos, while Image Flash 1.0 checks videos frame by frame. Both are available on the web, via API and in the Pangram Chrome extension, with claimed accuracy above 98% on the company's own tests.
